svg.title: Orbit-determination consistency with and without an injected model error
svg.desc: Consistency of an onboard Earth-GNSS orbit determination in a near-rectilinear halo orbit with an independent ground orbit determination, from real runs of engine v0.38.0 on scenarios/lunar-infrastructure-od-consistency.toml and the model-error variant (400 trials each). Mean normalised difference q is 5.81 with no model error and 5.95 with an injected acceleration error of 3e-10 m/s2, against 6 expected: the two orbit solutions are consistent (bar C1 MET). The share of trials above the 95 % point is 0.040 and 0.052; the bar for detecting the injected error was at least 0.5, so it is NOT MET (C3): the onboard solution is known to about 352 m against 23 m for the ground one, so a ten-metre displacement hides inside its covariance. MODELLED: a restricted three-body model with stated simplifications and illustrative inputs, not a measurement of any lunar quantity. Advisory: analysis output from a research and engineering tool, not type-approved navigation equipment and not a safety-of-life service.
